nodes.description: Base URI used to build token metadata URIs; writable by owner via setBaseURI.
Token metadata file extension (.json) appended in tokenURI.
Mint price in wei (0.06 ether), owner-adjustable via setCost and enforced in mint.
Maximum number of mintable tokens (5000); bounds mint and gates withdraw.
Percentage of contract balance paid as gift reward on mint; owner-adjustable.
block.timestamp + 15 days captured at deployment; time gate for owner withdraw.
Pause flag (default true) blocking mint until owner unpauses.
Reveal flag controlling whether tokenURI returns real metadata or placeholder.
Placeholder metadata URI returned before reveal.
Deploys ERC721 with name/symbol and initializes base URI and unrevealed URI.
Internal override returning the stored baseURI.
Payable mint function; computes supply, validates payment/pause/caller, computes and sends multiple reward payouts via low-level call, then safe-mints.
Pseudo-random generator from keccak256 of block.timestamp, msg.sender, _seed and _salt modulo _mod.
View helper returning all token IDs owned by an address.
Returns metadata URI depending on revealed state and baseURI/baseExtension.
Owner-only function to flip the revealed flag to true.
Owner-only setter for giftPercentage.
Owner-only setter for the mint cost.
Owner-only setter for the notRevealedUri placeholder.
Owner-only setter for the base URI.
Owner-only setter for baseExtension.
Owner-only function toggling the paused state.
Owner-only payable withdrawal of the full contract balance, gated by maxSupply or headStart timestamp.
Caller-controlled address used for caller checks, minting and payout recipient.
Miner-influenceable timestamp used for randomness seeds and the withdraw time gate.
Original transaction sender; not referenced in this contract.
Low-level payable call forwarding giftValue ETH to a pseudo-randomly selected or previous owner during mint, before state finalization.
Low-level payable call forwarding the entire contract balance to msg.sender in withdraw.
Predictable pseudo-randomness derived from block.timestamp and msg.sender used to pick payout recipients.

Constructor argument for the initial unrevealed URI.

edges.reason: Constructor calls setBaseURI to initialize the base URI.
Constructor calls setNotRevealedURI to initialize the placeholder URI.
setBaseURI writes the baseURI state variable.
setNotRevealedURI writes the notRevealedUri state variable.
_baseURI reads the baseURI state variable.
mint reads maxSupply to bound the token count.
mint reads cost to enforce the minimum payment.
mint reads paused to block minting when paused.
mint reads giftPercentage to compute the gift payout.
mint calls randomNum to choose payout recipients at various milestone supplies.
mint performs a low-level ETH transfer to an arbitrary recipient before finishing execution, enabling reentrancy into mint.
The low-level call transfers control to an external address that can re-enter mint.
tokenURI reads revealed to decide which metadata to return.
tokenURI reads baseExtension to build the metadata URI.
reveal writes the revealed state variable.
setGiftPercentage writes the giftPercentage state variable.
setCost writes the cost state variable.
setBaseExtension writes the baseExtension state variable.
pause writes the paused state variable.
withdraw reads maxSupply to gate withdrawal.
withdraw reads headStart as part of the time-based withdrawal gate.
withdraw performs a low-level ETH transfer of the whole balance to msg.sender, a reentrancy vector.
The low-level call hands control to an external address that can re-enter withdraw.
mint derives from msg.sender: requires it to differ from owner and mints to it.
withdraw sends the balance to msg.sender and relies on owner-based authorization.
msg.sender is the recipient of the low-level value transfer in withdraw.
randomNum seeds its pseudo-random value with block.timestamp (timestamp dependency).
headStart is initialized from block.timestamp at deployment (timestamp dependency).
mint passes block.timestamp into randomNum for recipient selection (timestamp dependency).
withdraw compares block.timestamp to headStart to authorize withdrawal (timestamp dependency).
randomNum executes the timestamp-derived pseudo-randomness operation.
block.timestamp feeds the predictable pseudo-random operation (timestamp dependency).
